items.entity: 2-D cantilever design domain (length L × height H)
items.description: Sec. II.1 and the Fig. 1a caption mention only a 'Design Domain' for a 'cantilever beam'. No dimensions or aspect ratio are given anywhere in the text; the shape appears only in Figs. 1a/1d, 2a–c and 3a. A rectangle is implied but never stated.

No element count, element size or element type is stated. Each 'site' is one element with density x_e (Sec. II.1; App. A uses N elements but gives no value). Figs. A1/A2 plot curves for 'all sites' and Fig. 3b/d maps individual sites, which points to a coarse grid that could only be counted from the unseen figures. Square bilinear (Q4) elements are assumed but not stated.

items.entity: fixed nodes (clamped end of the cantilever)
items.description: The Fig. 1a caption refers to 'Fixed Nodes' and Secs. II.1/II.3 to 'fixed nodes'/'fixed sites', but which edge and how much of it is fixed is shown only in Fig. 1a. The constrained DOFs are never listed; 'fixed' plus 'cantilever' implies full clamping (u_x = u_y = 0).
readings: whole left edge x = 0 (0 ≤ y ≤ H) clamped, u_x = u_y = 0
only a central segment of the left edge (e.g. 0.25H ≤ y ≤ 0.75H) clamped

items.entity: applied force on the free end
items.description: The text says only 'Applied Forces' (Fig. 1a caption) and 'load-bearing nodes/sites' (Secs. II.1, II.3). Where the load acts on the free edge is shown only in Fig. 1a.
readings: free edge x = L, bottom corner y = 0
free edge x = L, mid-height y = 0.5H
free edge x = L, top corner y = H

items.description: The plural wording ('Applied Forces' in Fig. 1a caption, 'load-bearing nodes' in Sec. II.1, 'load-bearing sites' in Sec. II.3) leaves open whether one nodal point load is used or the load is spread over several nodes or an edge segment. Nothing in the text quantifies it.
readings: load split equally over 2–3 adjacent nodes at the load point
uniform traction along the whole free edge

items.description: No direction is stated; only the arrow in Fig. 1a would show it. A transverse load is conventional for a cantilever. Flipping its sign gives an identical layout and compliance, but a non-vertical load would change the layout.
No magnitude is given. It scales compliance and so the absolute temperatures quoted 'in units of compliance' (T ≈ 20.7, 17.2, 3.3 in Sec. II.1), but not the optimal layout.

items.entity: Young's modulus of the solid phase E0
items.description: No modulus is given anywhere; Sec. IV.1/Eq. (3) speaks only of a strain-energy density. It scales compliance and the absolute T values.
readings: a physical value, e.g. E0 = 210 GPa

items.description: Not stated anywhere in the text.
The text never says whether the 2-D model is plane stress or plane strain, or what the out-of-plane thickness is. Plane strain changes the effective Poisson ratio; thickness only scales compliance.
Sec. II.1 lets densities run from 0 (void) to 1 (filled). That requires an ersatz void stiffness or a lower bound to keep the stiffness matrix non-singular, and none is given.

Compliance is written only as C = ∫ f(u(x),x) dV (Eq. 3, Sec. IV.1). No SIMP/RAMP law or exponent is given, either for the sampled ensembles or for the reference optimum of Fig. 3a ('as solved by [17]').
Appendix C says only that 'a density filter' is used, and Fig. A3 that it interacts with the boundaries. No radius is given, in element widths or physical units.

items.entity: filter type/kernel (incl. reference optimum of Fig. 3a)
items.description: App. C gives a density filter for the paper's own runs. Not stated: the kernel (linear cone vs. Gaussian/PDE), the edge treatment (Fig. A3 notes boundary effects), and whether the Fig. 3a optimum 'as solved by [17]' used the same density filter or a sensitivity filter. Elsewhere 'filter' means the Pareto-Laplace transform (Abstract, Secs. I, IV.2), not this regularization.
readings: linear-cone (hat) density filter, weights renormalized at domain edges
sensitivity filter of the same radius for the reference optimum

items.entity: densities on which V_f = 0.5 is enforced
items.description: V_f = 0.5 is stated (Sec. II.1). App. A enforces the constraint on the particle 'positions (densities)', while App. C adds a density filter. It is not said whether the constraint acts on raw design variables or on filtered (physical) densities.
readings: Σ x_e = 0.5·N on raw design variables

items.entity: optimizer, move limit and stopping criterion for the deterministic optimum
items.description: The optimized solution in Fig. 3a is 'as solved by [17]' with no settings given. Sec. IV.1 only says 'gradient-based algorithms'.
readings: OC update, move limit 0.2, damping 0.5, stop at max change < 0.01

items.description: The starting density field is not given, either for the conventional optimization or for the molecular-dynamics trajectories.

No passive regions are mentioned. Sec. II.1 says sites next to the fixed and load-bearing nodes condense as T drops, which implies they are design variables, but the text never states that the whole domain is designable.
readings: solid passive elements at the load point and/or the supports

items.description: Needed only to reproduce the thermostatted ensembles; a conventional solver gives the T→0 limit. Not given: the 'low' and 'high' T of Fig. 1d, the T grid, Nosé masses Q_k, chain length (written N_c, N_x and M in App. A; called a plain 'Nosé-Hoover' thermostat in Sec. II.1), time step, equilibration and sample count. T is only said to be 'in units of compliance'.
readings: low-T ensemble in the infill regime (T ≲ 3.3), high-T ensemble above 20.7 (e.g. T = 25 as in Fig. 4b)
low-T ensemble ≈ T → 0 (conventional optimum), high-T ensemble in the frame regime (3.3 ≲ T ≲ 17.2)

locator: Sec. II.1, the 2-D cantilever of Fig. 1
